content.comment_body: Good morning, I have a question about the relay output ampere rating and service life for [product_name] version [version_no]. I am using it to switch a hydraulic pump coil running on 24VDC. I don’t have the exact coil amperage, but it operates in multiple pulses per cycle. Thank you for your help.

The relevant specifications can be found in the system manual, including details on using inductive loads. Rather than quoting specific numbers, let me share my experience: we frequently use pneumatics, and have noticed that outputs on [product_name] often last less than 2 years, with some failing as quickly as within 2 months, even with currents below the stated limits. We now use external relays between the [product_name] output and the coil, sometimes using solid state relay banks. These are much cheaper to replace. You could also try using a diode in the circuit instead of an external relay. Hope these insights help.
Thank you for the advice regarding external relays. I agree this is a more practical approach when the coil type is not specified.

Hello, As [user_name] mentioned, and from my own experience, it is best to use external relays with [product_name] outputs. Otherwise, you may end up having to replace the entire [product_name] module instead of just a single relay.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users have observed that relay outputs in [product_name] modules may have a short service life when switching inductive loads like hydraulic pump coils, even if operating within specified limits. Several recommend installing external relays to protect the main module and reduce maintenance costs, indicating concerns over reliability in such scenarios.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are looking for reliable relay output operation with inductive loads and want to understand how long the outputs can be expected to last in these conditions.
